event_definitions: Tumor cells with optically clear cytoplasm arranged in compact nests or alveolar groups separated by delicate septa.
Neoplastic clear cells form small acini or tubules with recognizable central lumina.
Tumor cells cover branching or rounded fibrovascular cores to create a localized papillary configuration.
A localized tumor component is composed of compact cells with granular eosinophilic rather than optically clear cytoplasm.
Large discohesive tumor cells show eccentric nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and abundant dense eosinophilic cytoplasm.
A carcinoma component transitions into malignant spindle cells growing in intersecting fascicles or disordered sheets.
Tumor nuclei contain conspicuous eosinophilic nucleoli readily visible within enlarged vesicular nuclei.
A tumor region exhibits pronounced variation in nuclear size, shape, chromasia, and cellular form.
A localized viable tumor region contains numerous readily identifiable mitotic figures.
Tumor cells display abnormal multipolar, asymmetric, or otherwise malformed mitotic figures.
Geographic zones of dead tumor retain ghost-like architecture with eosinophilic cytoplasm and nuclear loss.
Extravasated erythrocytes and blood lakes dissect through or replace a localized tumor region.
A tumor region contains macroscopic or microscopic cyst-like spaces formed by degeneration and tissue loss.
A dense branching network of thin-walled capillaries courses between nests of clear tumor cells.
Cohesive tumor cells are present within endothelial-lined small vascular channels adjacent to or within the tumor.
A large venous lumen contains a cohesive expansile mass of viable renal carcinoma cells, often with associated fibrin or blood.
A compressed fibrous band forms a discrete boundary between the renal tumor and adjacent parenchyma.
Irregular tongues or nests of tumor traverse a pre-existing fibrous pseudocapsule into surrounding tissue.
Irregular carcinoma nests infiltrate among and replace native renal tubules or glomeruli at the tumor boundary.
Renal carcinoma nests or cords extend irregularly between adipocytes in perinephric fat.
Tumor extends into renal sinus soft tissue, fat, or vascular structures at the hilar interface.
Small irregular groups and cords of tumor cells separate from the main mass and permeate adjacent stroma.
Single tumor cells or tiny clusters detach from larger nests at an invasive tissue interface.
Small mature lymphocytes permeate viable tumor nests and directly contact carcinoma cells.
Dense localized aggregates of lymphocytes occupy stroma immediately outside the tumor boundary.
Lymphocytes accumulate in peritumoral stroma but remain largely absent from adjacent viable tumor nests.
A tumor region contains conspicuous aggregates of segmented neutrophils within viable tissue or at necrotic interfaces.
Activated fibroblastic stroma with newly deposited collagen surrounds and separates infiltrating tumor groups.
Dense paucicellular eosinophilic collagen forms broad scar-like bands within or adjacent to the tumor.
A loose pale stromal matrix with edema or myxoid quality separates tumor nests and contains sparse stellate cells.
